title: Function-word gaps
summary: Infer articles, pronouns, auxiliaries, prepositions and conjunctions from sentence structure and passage cohesion without relying on a word bank.

sections.title: Name the job before the word
content: Complete these frames aloud: “___ umbrella”, “waited ___ the rain stopped”, and “the book, ___ was damaged”. Notice that grammar narrows each blank before vocabulary does.
In open cloze, do not begin by guessing words. First name the missing word's job: article, pronoun, auxiliary, preposition or conjunction.

sections.title: Use the gap-role routine
content: Read the whole passage once so that you know the people, event order and main idea. Then read the words immediately before and after each gap.

Label the gap role. A singular countable noun may need an article; a repeated person or object may need a pronoun; a verb phrase may need an auxiliary; a fixed relationship may need a preposition; and two ideas may need a conjunction.
Insert one word and reread the complete sentence. Finally, reread the neighbouring sentence to check reference, time and logic.
Keep the answer narrow. The task rewards the exact defensible word or an explicitly approved alternative, not a broadly similar expression.

sections.title: Let structure constrain the answer
content: In “She opened ___ envelope”, envelope is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time. The vowel sound at the start of envelope selects “an”.
In “Nobody knew who ___ packed it”, packed is a past participle and the packing happened before the later discovery. The verb phrase therefore needs the auxiliary “had”.
In “the concert, ___ had taken place…”, the comma begins a non-defining relative clause about the concert. “Which” fits; “that” does not follow the comma in this structure.
When two forms are genuinely acceptable, such as “until” and “till” in an informal narrative, the reviewed answer set must name both before learners are scored.

sections.title: Annotate the evidence
content: For each gap, write A for article, Pn for pronoun, Aux for auxiliary, Prep for preposition or Conj for conjunction before entering a word.
Underline the smallest phrase that controls the answer. Draw an arrow to an earlier noun when a pronoun or relative word depends on reference.

sections.title: Complete the passage as one group
content: Read all four paragraphs of “The workshop box”. Supply exactly one word for each of the eight gaps without a word bank.
Do not check the answers one at a time. Complete every gap, reread the restored passage, then submit the group so that early feedback cannot reveal a later answer.

sections.title: Diagnose the open-cloze error
content: Gap role: I misidentified the type of function word the structure required.
Local grammar: I identified the word type but missed the construction immediately around the gap.
Cohesion clue: I overlooked reference, time or logic elsewhere in the sentence or passage.
Entry accuracy: I knew the word but entered an unapproved form or made a typing error. Record the closest cause before retrying.

sections.title: The workshop box
content: Complete one original open-cloze passage containing articles, pronouns, an auxiliary, prepositions and conjunctions. Feedback appears only after all eight gaps have an answer.
